text:
A: Hiya. Right, last one. Leanne.
B: Alison. Hello. You've got the cat on the filing cabinet.
A: Moth. She's there now actually, judging me. You've got a dog, haven't you? Everyone's been on about Biscuit.
B: Apparently he's famous. He's asleep under the table, which is all he does.
A: Where are you, then?
B: Tonbridge. Kent.
A: Stockport. Not Manchester. Don't say it.
B: I wasn't going to. I did geography at Sheffield, I'm aware there's more than one place up there.
A: Ha, fair. What do you do?
B: Planning, at the council.
A: Oh God. Right, so are you the people who let shop signs happen? Because I'm a graphic designer and the high street near me looks like someone sneezed a font catalogue at it.
B: Mostly no. Advertisement consent covers size and illumination, not taste. If it's not flashing at drivers, we can't refuse it for being ugly.
A: That's a scandal, that. There should be a font officer.
B: I'd apply. I'd turn down the meetings, though.
A: You'd be good at it. You've got a face that says no.
B: I've been told. It's useful at committee. People shout and I sort of just wait until they've finished.
A: See, I'd shout back. I told a client last week his logo looked like a 2009 Facebook page.
B: Did he change it?
A: He asked for someone else.
B: That's usually how it goes.
A: Yeah, well. I'd rather be doing my own prints anyway. Screen prints, zines. I used to skate roller derby, Moth to a Flame, but I've got rheumatoid arthritis now so it's swimming and printing.
B: That's a good name. Annoying, the arthritis, I'd imagine. More than annoying.
A: It's a pain. Literally. Some days I can't open a jar. Gavin has to do it and he's dead smug about it.
B: Graham does that with the crossword. Puts in the one I couldn't get and doesn't say anything. Which is worse.
A: Oh, the silent ones are worse. Do you read, then? You look like a reader.
B: Crime, mostly. Several at once. I don't finish half of them.
A: I do true crime podcasts. Same thing really, just with more adverts. Where do you go on holiday? Let me guess, cottage.
B: Pembrokeshire. Northumberland. You've got me.
A: I knew it. I'm city breaks. Berlin, Lisbon, Bologna. Flea markets and galleries.
B: I'd go to Bologna. For the arcades. My husband teases me for looking at street layouts.
A: That's actually quite cool. Don't tell anyone I said that. I thought you'd be a bit mardy from your photo.
B: I am a bit. I just keep it quiet. Anyway, I should think about dinner after this.
A: Tea. It's tea.
B: It's dinner, I'm afraid. I'm from Kent, I'm not —
